checks.explanation: The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act was signed into law in June 2022, less than two years after this prediction, ending a nearly 30-year federal stalemate on gun legislation with enhanced background checks for buyers under 21 and new funding for red-flag laws.

sources.title: Biden Signs Gun Bill Into Law, Ending Years of Stalemate

checks.explanation: The Fed held rates near zero for about two years, not five to ten, beginning its rate-hiking cycle in March 2022 in response to inflation that peaked at 9.1% and raising rates from 0-0.25% to 5.25-5.50% within about 17 months.

sources.title: A timeline of the Fed's '22-'23 rate hikes & what caused them

checks.explanation: The SPAC market did not consolidate around a small number of dominant, skilled sponsors; instead the entire market collapsed broadly starting in 2022 due to poor post-merger performance, SEC regulatory scrutiny, and an oversupply of novice sponsors, with even experienced sponsors seeing average de-SPAC'd companies down about 40% by late 2022.

sources.title: SPAC Market Report 2023: Highlights and Year-End Review

checks.explanation: California's police reform push did stall in 2020 as the pandemic cut the legislative session short, supporting the near-term 'laggard' framing, but the state came back in 2021 and passed sweeping reforms including the Police Decertification Act (California had been one of only four states without an officer decertification process) and a near-total chokehold ban, closing the gap with other reforming states rather than remaining a laggard.

sources.title: California's New, Sweeping Police Reform Legislation: What It Means and Why It Happened
